basis: Male reproductive infertility alone has no organ axis; endocrine dysfunction is not intrinsic to this umbrella concept.
Intellectual disability and cerebellar hypoplasia define the syndrome; strabismus impairs ocular alignment in 30–79%.
Proximal tubular dysfunction defines the disease; metabolic acidosis occurs in 28/28. Osteomalacia frequency is insufficiently established.
Hypospadias is a congenital malformation of the urethra, which belongs to the renal axis.
Myofibrillar skeletal myopathy and cardiomyopathy define the disease. Hepatomegaly alone does not establish hepatic damage; tremor and clonus do not establish separate neural damage.
Inherited retinal degeneration causes night blindness, impaired color vision, scotomas and reduced visual acuity.
Knuckle pads are localized fibrous thickening of skin and subcutis over joints; underlying joint or bone damage is not intrinsic.
Nematode infection; neural larva migrans causes lasting CNS injury in most recognized clinical cases (>30%). Ocular and visceral involvement vary.
TNNT2-related isolated dilated cardiomyopathy directly affects myocardium, with frequent ventricular dysfunction and heart failure.
Papillary adenoma originates in the kidney.
Neurodevelopmental disorder; contractures, muscle atrophy and kyphoscoliosis occur in 2/2 assessed, as do astigmatism and esotropia. Pigment marks do not establish skin damage.
Pontocerebellar malformation and severe developmental impairment define disease. Neutropenia and thrombocytopenia each occur in 2/9 (<30%).
Bone fragility, osteopenia, recurrent fractures and skeletal deformity define disease. Blue sclerae are uncommon and do not establish visual impairment.
Clonal marrow disease with excess myeloid blasts and ineffective hematopoiesis. Progression to acute leukemia is a separate disease.
SAG-related retinal dysfunction causes congenital stationary night blindness.
Lysosomal lipid catabolism/storage disorder. Specific neurologic, hepatic and other organ damage varies substantially across this broad umbrella.
Inherited interstitial lung disease with characteristic brain calcifications defines this pulmonary and cerebral syndrome.
Congenital duplication of a biphalangeal thumb is a skeletal malformation.
Ichthyosis and male hypogonadism define skin disease and deficient gonadal endocrine function.
Anterior segment dysgenesis defines eye disease; hydrocephalus/encephalocele and severe sensorineural hearing loss each affect 1/3 (~33%). Small pituitary lacks proven dysfunction.
Primary skeletal muscle disease causes distal weakness and atrophy. Neuromuscular classification does not establish nerve disease.
Pituitary growth hormone deficiency with possible hypothyroidism defines endocrine disease; enlarged sella alone does not establish skeletal dysfunction.
Cystine storage causes renal Fanconi disease; corneal crystal keratopathy affects nearly all, rickets 2/3. Myopathy 22/86 and cerebral calcification 9/33 fall below 30%.
Tumor originates in ovary or testis; reproductive tumor origin alone does not establish endocrine gland dysfunction.
Epithelial adenoma originates in the gallbladder, which belongs to the hepatic axis.
